target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial aviation excluding unlawful acts
evidence.observation: IATA reports five fatal accidents in 2020: three jet and two turboprop. The three fatal jets account for 121 onboard fatalities: Pakistan International Airlines A320 (97), Pegasus B737-800 (3), and Air India Express B737-800 (21). IATA separately reports one fatality not onboard an aircraft and explicitly excludes unlawful acts from its 132-fatality accident total.
evidence.use: annual fatal-jet universe, Boeing/non-Boeing membership mapping for non-boundary cases, and source-scope evidence

evidence.publisher: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), United States
evidence.authority_role: ICAO Annex 13 accredited representative for State of Design/Manufacture
evidence.observation: NTSB records Pegasus Airlines flight PC2193, Boeing 737-800, runway excursion at Istanbul Sabiha Gokcen with three passenger fatalities and identifies the Turkish investigation.

evidence.source_title: Final Investigation Report on Air India Express B737-800 VT-AXH accident
evidence.observation: AAIB records Air India Express B737-800 VT-AXH at Kozhikode as a landing runway-excursion accident with 21 fatalities.

evidence.publisher: Aircraft Accident Investigation Board of the Islamic Republic of Iran; copy hosted by ICAO
evidence.authority_role: state Annex 13 accident-investigation authority / ICAO-hosted final report
evidence.observation: The Annex 13 final report describes PS752 as an accident involving Boeing 737-800 UR-PSR and states that military activity interfering with civil aviation operations resulted in the accident.
evidence.use: competent-authority event evidence and target-semantics conflict

scope_issue.reason: The frozen target requires an accident involving a Boeing commercial jet with attributable fatality but does not prospectively specify whether an Annex 13 occurrence caused by unlawful/hostile action is included. The competent investigation calls PS752 an accident while IATA excludes it as an unlawful/security act. Choosing either convention now would be outcome-informed target redefinition.
scope_issue.required_resolution: A later target-taxonomy version may prospectively define the hostile/unlawful-action boundary for future forecasts, but it cannot retroactively open the 2014/2020 G1 cells for this historical validation without an independently pre-existing rule.

completeness_assessment.reason: The 2020 fatal-jet universe, non-boundary Boeing memberships and competent-authority evidence are complete. Only the hostile/unlawful-action target boundary for PS752 remains unresolved, so membership and taxonomy controls fail closed.

gate_effect: 2020 annual cell remains OPEN at 4/6; overall G1 remains BLOCKED
